reference.label: Position in the value array
reference.title: Change position in the value array
reference.prompt: The rules apply to all existing values, at least one value, a specific position, or the sum or length of the value array.
reference.legacy-help: Each rule needs a matching value. With AND, different values may satisfy different rules. This existing setting is preserved until you save another selection.
reference.any-open: At least one value must match
reference.any-help: Additional non-matching values prevent a match. Example: [matching, non-matching] → no match.
reference.any-open-help: Additional non-matching values are allowed. Example: [matching, non-matching] → match. Exception: With the “Empty input” rule, an empty array [] can also match.

derive-processing.TAKE_DISPLAYED_AS_ZERO_IF_PARTIAL: Treat displayed source responses as 0 after processing has started
derive-processing.TAKE_EMPTY_AS_ZERO_IF_PARTIAL: Treat empty invalid source responses as 0 after processing has started
derive-processing.TAKE_DISPLAYED_AS_ZERO_IF_PARTIAL_CONCAT: Replace displayed source responses with x after processing has started
derive-processing.TAKE_EMPTY_AS_ZERO_IF_PARTIAL_CONCAT_COD: Replace empty invalid source responses with x after processing has started
derive-processing.partial-credit-help: Replacement applies only within this derivation and requires at least one regularly coded response. Entirely unprocessed responses or only empty invalid responses are not scored automatically. Pending codings remain pending. Empty means null, empty text or an empty list; false and 0 are not empty responses.

solver-source-warning.unselected-sources: Warning: Variables referenced in the solver expression are not selected as source variables

solver-help.title: Syntax help for solver expressions
solver-help.description: Solver expressions are evaluated with math.js. Use numbers, operators and math.js functions; refer to source variables with ${VariableName} or ${VariableID}.
solver-help.policy-description: Optionally specify a fragment index and how empty or non-numeric values are handled. Available policies are INC, ERROR, or a numeric replacement value; ERROR is the default.

examples.variables: add values from two source variables
examples.condition: condition: result is 1 when points are at least 5, otherwise 0
examples.fragment: use the numerator (fragment 0) of a fraction; mark empty values incomplete and non-numeric values as errors (equivalent to ${Bruch[0]:INC:ERROR})
examples.policies: use a summand; replace empty values with 0 and mark non-numeric values incomplete
